title: Prepositions
summary: The small words that place things in time and space — "at 5 PM", "on Monday", "for five years".
whyThisTopic: Bangla uses postpositions that don't line up one-to-one with English, so these are the words that go wrong most often and are noticed most quickly.

lessons.title: at, on, in — largest to smallest

blocks.text: Three prepositions cover almost every time expression, and they narrow from large to small: **in** for long periods, **on** for days and dates, **at** for exact times.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা

lessons.title: How long, since when, by when

blocks.text: These prepositions answer three different questions. **for** measures how long. **since** names the point it started from. **by** sets a deadline, and **until** means right up to a moment without stopping.

items.text: I have worked here for three days.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: **since five years** is the commonest mistake here. **since** needs a point in time — *since 2021*, *since Monday*. A length of time takes **for** — *for five years*.

lessons.title: in, on, at — and what sits where

blocks.text: **in** puts something inside a space, **on** puts it on a surface, and **at** marks a point — a place you think of as a spot rather than an area.
in a space  →  on a surface

rows: in the room, in Dhaka, in the box

at the door, at the station, at the wedding

items.text: The letters are in the drawer.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: **under** is directly beneath something. **between** needs exactly two things — *between the bank and the hospital* — while **among** needs a group of more than two.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: কোনো স্থানের ভেতরে হলে **in** (in the room), কোনো তলের উপরে হলে **on** (on the table), আর নির্দিষ্ট একটি বিন্দু বোঝাতে **at** (at the gate)। বাস-ট্রেনে **on** বসে — **on the bus**, *in the bus* নয়। **between** ঠিক দুটির মাঝে, আর **among** দুইয়ের বেশি একটি দলের মধ্যে।

lessons.title: Where to, where from, which path

blocks.text: Movement prepositions answer three questions. **to** gives the destination and **from** the origin. **into** and **out of** cross a boundary. **across** and **through** describe the path taken.
to = where it ends up

items.text: He came out of the building.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: **across** is for a flat surface — *across the road*. **through** means going inside something and out the far side — *through the tunnel*, *through the forest*.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: গন্তব্য বোঝাতে **to**, উৎস বোঝাতে **from**। ভেতরে ঢুকলে **into**, বের হলে **out of**। বাংলা থেকে দুইটি ভুল খুব সাধারণ: *He went in the market* — সঠিক **went to the market**; আর *She entered into the room* — **enter**-এর পরে কিছু বসে না, **entered the room** হবে। পথ বোঝাতে সমতল কিছুর উপর দিয়ে হলে **across**, ভেতর দিয়ে হলে **through**।

practice.prompt: He is going ___ Dhaka next week.

feedback.en: Correct. The destination takes **to**.
feedback.bn: ঠিক আছে। গন্তব্য বোঝাতে **to** বসে।

feedback.en: **at** marks where something stays. The place it is heading takes **to**.
feedback.bn: **at** কোথায় থাকে তা বোঝায়। কোথায় যাচ্ছে বোঝাতে **to** বসে।

feedback.en: **from** names the origin. The destination takes **to**.
feedback.bn: **from** কোথা থেকে বোঝায়। গন্তব্য বোঝাতে **to** বসে।

feedback.en: **in** says where something already **is**. Movement to a place takes **to** — *go to the market*, never *go in the market*.
feedback.bn: **in** কোথায় **আছে** তা বোঝায়। কোথাও যাওয়া বোঝাতে **to** বসে — *go to the market*, *go in the market* নয়।

lessons.title: by the method, with the tool

blocks.text: **by** says *how* — the method, the means of travel, or the person who did it. **with** says what you held in your hand while doing it.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: Look at the article. **by** + a method takes none — *by bus*, never *by a bus*. **with** + a tool needs one — *with a knife*, never *with knife*.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: উপায় বা যানবাহন বোঝাতে **by** — *by bus*, *by email*; এর পরে কোনো article বসে না। হাতে ধরা যন্ত্র বোঝাতে **with** — *with a knife*; এখানে article লাগে। Passive-এ যে কাজটি করেছে তার আগেও **by** বসে। দুইটি সাধারণ ভুল: *I came with bus* — সঠিক **by bus**; আর *She cut it by a knife* — সঠিক **with a knife**।

lessons.title: The word decides, not the meaning

blocks.text: Some prepositions are not chosen by meaning at all. They belong to the word in front of them. **interested** always takes **in**; **depend** always takes **on**. These are learned as pairs, not worked out.

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: Bangla often suggests a different preposition. *Interested on*, *depend of*, *afraid from*, *reason of* and *married with* are all common — and all wrong.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: এখানে preposition অর্থ দেখে বাছাই হয় না — আগের শব্দটিই ঠিক করে দেয়। **interested**-এর সাথে **in**, **depend**-এর সাথে **on**, **belong**-এর সাথে **to**। এগুলো জোড়া হিসেবে মনে রাখতে হয়। বাংলা থেকে আসা সাধারণ ভুল: *interested on*, *depend of*, *afraid from*, *reason of*, *married with*।

lessons.title: When English needs nothing at all

blocks.text: Some English verbs take their object directly, with nothing in between — even where Bangla puts a word there. Adding a preposition to these is one of the most noticeable mistakes a learner can make.
discuss the problem

blocks.label: Watch out
blocks.text: **arrive** is the exception. **reach** takes nothing — *reach Dhaka* — but **arrive** needs a preposition: *arrive at the station*, *arrive in Dhaka*.

blocks.label: ব্যাখ্যা
blocks.text: কিছু ইংরেজি verb-এর পরে সরাসরি object বসে, মাঝে কোনো preposition লাগে না — যদিও বাংলায় একটি শব্দ থাকে। **discuss**, **enter**, **reach**, **request**, **investigate** — এদের পরে কিছু বসে না। **home**, **abroad**, **upstairs**-এর আগেও **to** বসে না: **go home**, *go to home* নয়। তবে **arrive** ব্যতিক্রম — এর পরে **at** বা **in** লাগে।
